tier_reason: COMPARISON.md and its public harness (async/bench/compare/bench_compare.cpp, Google Benchmark, enabled with -DTAP_SR_BUILD_COMPARE_BENCH=ON) state GCC 13.3 -O3 (CMake Release, no -march), but the host CPU is only a 'shared Xeon @ 2.10 GHz' with no model, so the timed numbers miss tier A; they are the project author's own measurements (first-party), hence C. The embedded rows are reproducible QEMU instruction counts (.github/workflows/compare.yml, async/bench/icount/cmp_main.cpp, pinned arm-none-eabi-gcc 13.2.1 and hexagon-clang 19.1.5 at -O3), but they count instructions rather than time, and the same author ran them.

corrections.claimed_speedup: COMPARISON.md (host x86, 2026-09-25, million output frames/s, median of 5) reports SampleRateTap 3.1-3.9x faster than libsamplerate 0.2.2 (stereo/mono; 1.5x at 8 channels) at the ~120 dB tier and 6.1x at the ~140 dB tier, with about 2-3.6x less latency. Table rows: balanced vs libsamplerate MEDIUM: mono 20.3 vs 5.2, stereo 14.6 vs 4.8, 8-ch 3.0 vs 1.9; transparent vs libsamplerate BEST: stereo 9.6 vs 1.6. Latency is 24 vs 46 frames (MEDIUM) and 40 vs 143 frames (BEST). The tiers are paired by vendor-stated stopband depth only. On the same page SampleRateTap is SLOWER than soxr HQ (114.3 mono, 52.9 stereo, 12.9 8-ch) and r8brain-free-src 120 dB (35.4 mono, 16.5 stereo, 4.1 8-ch). In embedded steady-state instruction counts (QEMU, stereo, 32-frame blocks), libsamplerate MEDIUM executes 2.7x (Cortex-M55), 3.2x (Cortex-M33) and 3.3x (Hexagon) more instructions per output frame than SampleRateTap balanced float, and BEST executes 7.8-9.8x more.
corrections.workload: A fixed, known near-unity ratio (48000 to 48009.6 Hz, 1 + 200 ppm) applied to a 997 Hz float sine streamed in 128-frame blocks, for mono, stereo and 8-channel streams, measured in million output frames per second. SampleRateTap runs only its fractional_resampler datapath with a constant rate deviation; the servo is quiescent and clock recovery is not timed. libsamplerate gets the ratio through src_process. Algorithmic latency is also reported. The embedded rows count QEMU executed instructions per stereo output frame (32-frame blocks; 2 s and 4 s runs separate steady-state from construction cost).
corrections.compiler_and_flags: GCC 13.3 -O3 (CMake Release; the bench target adds only warning flags, no -march). libsamplerate 0.2.2 and soxr 0.1.3 are the Ubuntu 24.04 distro packages, so their build flags are the distro's. r8brain-free-src is at pinned commit 7.5 with Ooura FFT. Embedded counts: arm-none-eabi-gcc 13.2.1 and hexagon-clang 19.1.5 at -O3 (CMake Release).
corrections.hardware: Host: shared Xeon @ 2.10 GHz (exact model not stated), run 2026-09-25. Embedded: QEMU TCG instruction counting on Cortex-M55 (mps3-an547), Cortex-M33 (mps2-an505) and Hexagon (qemu-hexagon 8.2.2) via the manually triggered compare.yml workflow.
corrections.caveats: First-party: the harness and doc are by the project's author. On x86 host throughput, SampleRateTap beats only libsamplerate; soxr HQ and r8brain-free-src are faster (the author says so openly) but carry 8-33x more latency. The host CPU model is not stated (shared Xeon), and no raw result file is committed; the numbers exist only in COMPARISON.md. The libsamplerate latency rows date from 2026-06-12. The tiers are matched on stopband depth only, so the engines do not do equal filtering work. SampleRateTap balanced is 48 taps with a 20 kHz passband and a 28 kHz stopband edge, above the 24 kHz Nyquist (async/include/tap/sr/async/polyphase_filter.h). libsamplerate MEDIUM is 120.61 dB with a 90% -3 dB bandwidth and about 91 taps per output at this ratio (half length 22437, increment 491 in src/mid_qual_coeffs.h; tap count derived from source data). At the ~140 dB tier, SampleRateTap transparent is 80 taps (20-26 kHz transition, 140 dB), while libsamplerate BEST's table is 154.67 dB at about 286 taps (derived from source data). Part of the speedup therefore comes from a shorter filter with a wider transition band, which lets 20-24 kHz content alias above 20 kHz. No THD+N was measured for libsamplerate MEDIUM. The THD+N table pairs SampleRateTap balanced (-133.9 dB at 24-bit I/O, servo recovering the clock) with libsamplerate sinc_best (-143.5 dB, fed the exact ratio), about 10 dB better. The products solve different problems: the async engine is an ASRC limited to near-unity ratios (default +/-1000 ppm), while libsamplerate is a general fixed-ratio converter (1/256 to 256). The benchmark times only the fixed-ratio datapath, so the clock recovery the libraries lack is not timed, and SampleRateTap cannot replace libsamplerate outside drift correction. On embedded targets, construction costs far more than libsamplerate (870 M vs 20.9 M instructions on Cortex-M33 for balanced vs MEDIUM). The benchmarks are behind TAP_SR_BUILD_COMPARE_BENCH (requires TAP_SR_BUILD_BENCHMARKS), off by default. The repo is young (5 stars, 225 commits, measurements back to June 2026, no issues filed); no correctness bug behind the numbers was found.

notes: The page numbers match the record. The doc's ratios agree with its tables to within rounding of the displayed values: 14.6/4.8 = 3.04 and 3.0/1.9 = 1.58 (derived from page data), against the stated 3.1x and 1.5x. The main shortcoming is the quality pairing: the tiers are matched by stopband dB, while libsamplerate's filters keep the transition band below Nyquist with roughly 2x (MEDIUM) and 3.5x (BEST) the taps. The ASRC also solves only the near-unity drift problem, not general rate conversion.
